extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and readers interested in media studies and Glasgow Media Group publications
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts implicit and explicit quality criteria for media studies research and books as illustrated by the Glasgow Media Group's book descriptions. Focuses on methodological, theoretical, and substantive standards implied by the descriptions (e.g., audience research, content analysis, case studies, interdisciplinarity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine media coverage and its impact on public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies should examine media coverage of events and the impact it has on public opinion (e.g., "examines media coverage of the current conflict in the Middle East and the impact it has on public opinion").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include analysis of how news content shapes audience beliefs; explore mechanisms by which images or narratives affect public understanding (the page notes exploration of the impact through new audience research and how controlling audience beliefs can reduce the impact of images of war).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze differential representation of conflicting parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and illustrate major differences in the way opposing groups are represented, including how casualties are shown and presentation of motives and rationales of both sides (e.g., "illustrate major differences in the way Israelis and Palestinians are represented, including how casualties are shown and the presentation of the motives and rationales of both sides").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coded content analysis and case examples to show representational bias and omissions; compare visual and verbal framing across parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include focused case studies of major news events
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific case studies of how television/newspapers covered major events (e.g., Israeli attack on Gaza, Gaza flotilla, Falklands War, Miners' Strike) to reveal patterns in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case studies should examine coverage during discrete events to reveal promotional strategies, PR influence, selection, and framing; link event coverage to broader media practices and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use large or substantive audience research samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ substantial audience research (the site cites an audience sample of over 800 people) to connect media content with audience understanding, beliefs and attitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine quantitative samples with qualitative methods to assess how exposure translates into beliefs and attitudes; report sample size and sampling approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct detailed, longitudinal content analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform detailed analysis of news content over extended periods (e.g., the site references "a detailed analysis of TV news over a two-year period").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longitudinal analysis helps reveal persistent patterns and change over time; document coding schemes, units of analysis, and temporal scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give a clear exposition of methods and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a transparent, clear exposition of methods and results as a main focus ("The main focus of the book is on giving a clear exposition of our methods and results").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe data collection, analysis procedures, limitations, and how conclusions were reached; separate empirical findings from broader theoretical discussion where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use focus-group methodologies for audience research
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply focus group methods to study audience beliefs and responses (the site references "focus group methodologies for audience research").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use focus groups to probe meanings, interpretations, and the processes by which viewers make sense of images and narratives; report facilitation and analysis techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine production processes, promotional strategies and meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze promotional strategies of interest groups, the production of media coverage, meanings promoted by the media, and their impact on policy and society (e.g., "examines the promotional strategies of interest groups, the production of media coverage, meanings promoted by the media and their impact on policy culture and society").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate organizational, commercial and PR influences on content; study how production routines, sources, and institutional settings shape news messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on structures and pressures rather than individual blame
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid simply 'monitoring' or criticising individual journalists; instead discuss the pressures and structures within which they work to show effects on news content ("our intention was not to ‘monitor’ the media or to criticise individual journalists. Our intention was to discuss the pressures and structures within which they work").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame critique at institutional and systemic levels (ownership, commercial pressures, legal/regulatory context) rather than targeting individuals; link structural factors to content outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary, empirically engaged scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce research that is empirically engaged and draws on multiple disciplines (the site highlights contributions from sociology, politics, geography, philosophy, economics, etc., and criticises avoidance of empirical work by some academics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine empirical methods with theoretical insight; prefer research that engages real-world problems and policy implications over purely abstruse theoretical debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent, critical research that reveals policy effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct independent research capable of criticising political policies and revealing their social effects ("point to the need for independent research which can criticise political policies and reveal their effects").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect media analysis to broader social and policy consequences; be explicit about normative implications and possible reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine images and stigmatization and their social impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the content of media images (e.g., mental conditions) showing how they are depicted and stigmatised, and consider the impact on public beliefs, carers and service users ("examines the content of media images of mental conditions ... showing how these are routinely depicted and stigmatised").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze visual framing, language, and recurring tropes; assess downstream impacts on stigma, service provision, and public attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider ownership, roots of media power and political effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine development, issues of ownership, and roots of media power in public and political spheres ("examine the development, issues of ownership, and roots of media power in the public and political spheres").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study commercial and legal structures, market forces, and political relationships that shape what media can and do publish; link to consequences for democracy and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical/chronological overview to assess competing narratives
rubrics_metrics.description: Present contending viewpoints in historical order and indicate which are based on considered historical evidence (as done in the overview of Zionist movement and subsequent events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chronological framing to trace emergence of narratives and test them against primary sources and scholarly debate; clarify evidence basis for competing histories.
